messages:
Ben: ran a quick mobile audit of the console UI at 375px and 320px. main problems: nav behavior overlaps table header + several action buttons are < 44px. attaching screenshots.
Mina: thanks. I noticed the table header gets hidden when the nav opens and you can no longer see column labels while scrolling.
Sasha: is the nav implemented as a full overlay sheet or a transform: translateX? both have implications for focus and stacking contexts.
Evan: current branch uses translateX with body scroll locked. on really small widths (<= 340) layout math misdetects and it leaves 16px of whitespace, pushing the table right.
Ravi: accessibility: if you trap focus inside the nav, we need an announced close button and restore focus to the invoking control. also ensure `aria-hidden` on the main content when overlay is active.
Mina: also found touch target problem on the per-row action icons. we should increase hit area with a transparent padding element so icons remain visually small but hit area >=44px.
Ben: design idea 1201: collapse non-essential columns at small breakpoints and expose them in a per-row overflow panel (not just horizontal scroll). preserves primary columns and reduces accidental horizontal pan.
Sasha: agree. propose a priority list: id, name, state, last-run, actions. optional columns move into overflow. we should show a summary pill on collapsed rows to indicate hidden info.
Evan: implementation note: we can server-annotate column priority for heavy table queries so initial render is compact on small clients. fallback: let CSS horizontal scroll when JS fails.
Ravi: ARIA for the overflow menu: `role=menu` + `aria-label="Row options for {name}"`. ensure keyboard traps and `esc` closes and returns focus.
Mina: mock updated (attached). using left slide with 80% width on phones, backdrop + close chevron. header height 52px. when nav is open `inert` should be set on main to block screen readers.
Ben: copy q: change "Filters" label to "Refine" on narrow widths to save space. this is different from desktop. thoughts on translations?
Sasha: +1 but flag L10n: some languages expand. we should reserve space and test strings in German/Portuguese.
Evan: small CSS we can test quickly:
```
.table-row .touch-target { padding: 10px; margin: -10px; }
.table-wrap { overflow-x: auto; -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; }
.table thead { position: sticky; top: 52px; z-index: 50; background: var(--bg); }
```
Ravi: also test 200% zoom and RTL. sticky headers sometimes jump when direction changes.
QA-bot: checklist added: VoiceOver basic flow, TalkBack open/close gestures, 200% zoom, keyboard nav, i18n string length, touch target sizes.
Ben: UX question: bottom sheet for nav vs left slide. My leaning: left slide for primary nav (keeps map of sections). bottom sheet ok for contextual drawers.
Mina: agree. left slide with quick swipe to close is more discoverable for nav. bottom sheet feels odd for global nav.
Evan: will implement left slide overlay and add a small JS debounce to fix the mis-detect at <=340. will also wire the column-collapse behavior with a CSS class `.compact-columns`.
Sasha: I'll update mocks and include aria notes for the overflow menu and the nav close control.
Ravi: I'll run accessibility pass once dev PR is up. add me as reviewer.
Ben: action items: Evan to PR with overlay + compact collapse + CSS snippet, Sasha to update mocks and i18n file, Ravi to run a11y checks, Mina to validate touch-target adjustments. deadline: next Wed EOD.
design-bot: reminder: mobile UX review scheduled Wed 11:00 in #design. :spiral_calendar:
Mina: thanks everyone, filing follow-ups in the ticket and will link here. :thumbsup:
